UK Passport Photo Requirements at a Glance

A UK passport photo is 35 × 45 mm when printed, with a head height of 29–34 mm, and at least 600 × 750 pixels when digital. Use a plain, light-coloured background, face the camera with a neutral expression, and take the photo within the last month. Not sure yours qualifies?   • Background: plain cream or light grey for printed photos. Never white, patterned or shadowed.
  • Pose: face forward, mouth closed, eyes open, no smile.
  • Age: taken in the last month.

UK Passport Photo Rules: Your Checklist

HM Passport Office rejects photos that break any of these rules. Check each point before you apply.

  • Face fully visible: keep hair away from your eyes. Do not wear hats or cover your face. Religious or medical head coverings are allowed if your full face stays visible.
  • Plain expression: keep your mouth closed and look straight at the camera. Do not smile.
  • Eyes open and clear: avoid red eye, glare and shadows across your eyes.
  • Glasses: avoid them. If you must wear them, use clear lenses with no glare, reflections or frames covering your eyes.
  • Even light: light your face evenly. Shadows on your face or behind you cause rejection.
  • Alone in the photo: no other people or objects.
  • Sharp and unedited: use a clear, focused colour photo with no filters or retouching.
  • Recent: take it within the last month.

How to Check and Fix Your UK Passport Photo in 3 Steps

  1. Upload your photo: choose a JPEG, PNG or HEIC file from your phone or camera.
  2. Review the automatic checks: the tool tests head position, background, lighting and resolution, then fixes what it can.
  3. Download your file: save a digital photo for your online application, or a 6 × 4 inch sheet with four photos for printing.

Want a pass or fail result first? Run the free UK passport photo checker. To take the photo yourself, follow our guides to taking a passport photo at home and taking one with an iPhone.

Common Reasons UK Passport Photos Get Rejected

  • Shadows or uneven light: stand facing a window and avoid overhead lamps.
  • Wrong background: use plain light grey or cream, not white or a patterned wall.
  • Glare on glasses: remove your glasses or tilt the camera slightly down.
  • Smiling or open mouth: relax your face and close your mouth.
  • Self-cropped digital photo: upload the full photo and let GOV.UK crop it.
  • Filters and retouching: turn off beauty modes and HDR.

UK Passport Photo Requirements for Babies and Children

Children must be alone in the photo. Under-6s do not need to look at the camera or keep a plain expression. Under-1s do not need open eyes. Lay a baby on a plain, light-coloured sheet and photograph them from above. Babies must not hold toys or use dummies. For step-by-step tips, see our UK child and baby passport photo guide.

Printing Your Passport Photos

Print on plain photo paper with no borders, creases or marks. Use our 4 × 6 inch passport photo template for a ready-made sheet, or read how to print passport photos for lab and home options.

Frequently Asked Questions About UK Passport Photo Requirements

What size is a UK passport photo?

A printed UK passport photo measures 35 mm wide by 45 mm tall (3.5 × 4.5 cm, or about 1.38 × 1.77 inches). A digital photo must be at least 600 pixels wide and 750 pixels tall.

What is the UK passport photo size in inches?

35 × 45 mm equals roughly 1.38 × 1.77 inches. The aspect ratio is 7:9.

What size must a digital UK passport photo be?

At least 600 × 750 pixels, between 50 KB and 10 MB, in colour, clear and in focus, and unaltered by software. Do not crop it yourself, because GOV.UK crops it for you.

What background colour does a UK passport photo need?

A plain, light-coloured background with clear contrast to your face and hair. For printed photos, choose cream or light grey. White is not accepted, and shadows, patterns and objects are not allowed.

How big should my head be in a UK passport photo?

For a printed photo, your head must measure 29–34 mm from chin to crown. For a digital photo, show your head, shoulders and upper body. GOV.UK crops the image to the right size.

Can I wear glasses in a UK passport photo?

Avoid glasses if you can. If you must wear them, the lenses cannot be tinted, and frames, glare, reflections or shadows must not cover your eyes. Sunglasses are never accepted.

Can I smile in a UK passport photo?

No. Keep a plain expression, with your mouth closed and your eyes open and visible. Look straight at the camera.

How recent must my passport photo be?

Take it within the last month. You need a new photo for every new passport, even if you look the same.

How many printed photos do I need for a UK passport?

Paper applications need two identical printed photos. Online applications need one digital photo, or a code from a photo booth or shop.

Does the UK government check my passport photo?

Yes. HM Passport Office checks every photo, and a photo that breaks the rules delays your application. GOV.UK says booth and shop photos are more likely to be approved than photos taken on your own device.

Can I check my UK passport photo for free before I apply?

Yes. Use our free UK passport photo checker to test head position, background, lighting and expression before you submit. It shows which checks pass and which fail.

What are the passport photo requirements for babies and children?

Children must be alone in the photo. Under-6s do not need to look at the camera or keep a plain expression. Under-1s do not need open eyes. Lay a baby on a plain, light-coloured sheet and photograph them from above. Babies must not hold toys or use dummies.

Use our print-ready 6 × 4 inch passport photo template after you fix your photo. It places four correctly sized photos on one sheet for home printing or a photo lab.

What Is an ICAO Standard Photograph?

In short: an ICAO standard photograph is a passport-style portrait that follows the International Civil Aviation Organization biometric rules (Doc 9303): a plain light background, a neutral expression, open eyes, and a fixed head size, so border and e-gate systems can read your face. It is usually 35 × 45 mm (413 × 531 px at 300 DPI).

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) sets the global biometric photo standard used by passport authorities, visa offices, and airport identity systems around the world. An ICAO standard photograph follows strict rules for head size, eye position, background color, lighting, and image sharpness so that facial recognition software can read it accurately at border control. You can test any image against these rules with this free ICAO standard photo checker, and if a portal has rejected yours, this guide explains why a photo is not valid as per ICAO standard and how to fix it. Most countries base their national passport photo rules directly on ICAO standards, which is why a photo that meets ICAO specifications is accepted almost everywhere. Our tool builds a fully compliant ICAO standard photograph from any photo you upload, in under a minute, with no design software required.

How to Convert Your Photo to ICAO Standard — 3 Steps

You do not need to understand the technical specifications yourself. The tool applies them for you.

  1. Choose Your Document: Select the passport, visa, or ID type you need. The tool loads the exact ICAO-based profile for that document, including biometric ratios, background color, and resolution.
  2. Upload a Photo: Upload an existing photo or take a new one with your phone. JPEG, PNG, and WEBP files up to 15 MB work, from a camera roll, scanner, or gallery.
  3. Auto-Correct and Download: The tool removes the background, replaces it with the required color, aligns your face to the ICAO grid, and checks lighting and sharpness before you download the finished photo.

ICAO Photo Size and Specifications

These are the measurements an ICAO standard photo is built around. Exact print size and background shade vary by country, so always confirm with the authority that reviews your application.

RequirementICAO-based standard
Print size35 × 45 mm (most common). ICAO defines proportions, so some countries use another print size, for example 2 × 2 in in the US.
Digital size413 × 531 px at 300 DPI (35 × 45 mm)
Head height (chin to crown)About 70–80% of photo height, which is 32–36 mm on a 45 mm photo
Eye lineRoughly 50–60% of the way up from the bottom edge, with the head centred
ResolutionAt least about 90 pixels between the centres of the eyes; sharp, in focus, no pixelation
BackgroundPlain, uniform and light (white or light grey). No pattern, texture or shadows
ExpressionNeutral, mouth closed, both eyes open and looking at the camera

Colour and retouchingNatural colour, no filters, no heavy retouching

Source: ICAO Doc 9303 (Part 3) and ISO/IEC 19794-5 face image standard. See the official references below.

Core Requirements of an ICAO Standard Photograph

ICAO photo standards exist to make sure a photo works both for a human officer at a counter and for automated facial recognition at an e-gate. The tool checks every one of these points automatically.

  • Head Position and Size: ICAO defines the exact proportion of the frame your head should occupy, measured from chin to crown. The tool uses facial landmark detection to align and crop your photo to this ratio precisely.
  • Neutral Background: A plain, evenly lit background — usually white or light grey — is a core ICAO requirement, since shadows or texture can confuse recognition software. The tool removes your original background and replaces it automatically.
  • Even, Shadow-Free Lighting: ICAO standards reject photos with shadows on the face or background. The tool detects lighting imbalance and corrects it so the final image is uniformly lit.
  • Neutral Expression, Open Eyes: A neutral expression with both eyes open and visible is required under ICAO guidelines. The tool flags photos with closed eyes, tilted heads, or exaggerated expressions so you can retake them if needed.
